title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: The post-election calm in oil lasted one day: Iran reported more tankers hit in Hormuz on Thursday and Brent jumped back to $98. In the air, Saudi routes stay cut, and Emirates SkyCargo shows how much the capacity squeeze is worth: cargo revenue up about half on flat volumes.

gauges.label: Brent crude, per barrel
gauges.note: Up $3.67 (3.9%) on Thursday after tanker attacks, after an 8%+ fall on Wednesday (Reuters, 5 Nov)

gauges.label: Vessels hit in the Gulf in October
gauges.note: Most of any month of the war; 5+ more since Sunday (UKMTO via Reuters, 5 Nov)

gauges.label: UAE non-oil PMI, October
gauges.note: Down from 55.3; output prices rose at the fastest rate since 2009 (S&P Global via The National)

gauges.label: Emirates SkyCargo cargo revenue, Apr–Sep
gauges.note: On 1.24m tonnes, down 1%; capacity squeeze lifts yields (Air Cargo News, 5 Nov)

gauges.label: UAE diesel per litre, November
gauges.note: Down from Dh4.80 in October; petrol down Dh0.24 (Gulf News, 31 Oct)

stories.headline: Iran says five tankers and a tug caught fire in Hormuz; attacks keep October's record pace
body: Iranian forces say at least five tankers were damaged on Thursday, some by naval mines, and a tug caught fire while helping a burning supertanker. UKMTO separately reported a tanker hit by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar late on Wednesday.

UKMTO counts at least five vessels with incidents since Sunday, the same pace as October, when 35 vessels were hit. It says it is struggling to report attacks accurately because most ships no longer report them. Talks through Qatari mediators continue with no breakthrough.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: strikes now reach inside the Gulf off Qatar, not just near Oman. Sea war-risk surcharges stay, and Gulf-wide routings carry risk.
stories.source: Al Jazeera; Reuters via BOE Report

stories.headline: Oil bounces back to $98 as the attacks resume
body: Brent settled up $3.67, or 3.9%, at $98.29 on Thursday. WTI rose 2.7% to $90.52. Both had fallen more than 8% on Wednesday after the US midterms.
Eurasia Group now puts the chance of a deal at 10%, down from 20%, and a prolonged standoff at 30%, up from 15%. It still sees a 60% chance of renewed US strikes, which could push Brent to $110–$125.
stories.soWhat: Yesterday's oil fall has partly reversed. Do not rush fuel surcharge cuts; model December at $95–$100 with an upside case.

stories.headline: Saudi air links stay cut; Etihad's Jeddah flights return today
body: Etihad's Riyadh and Dammam passenger and cargo flights stay cancelled to 19 November, but EY601–604 to Jeddah resume today, 6 November. Emirates cancelled more Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah flights on Thursday, and Air Arabia cut Riyadh, Abha and Jizan services from Sharjah.

Foreign carriers are out for longer: IndiGo and Air India to 14 November, Lufthansa from Riyadh to 18 November and Dammam to 30 November, KLM to 27 November, Cathay Pacific from Riyadh to 31 January. Saudia and flyadeal are routing some Riyadh services through Qassim with bus transfers.
stories.soWhat: New: Jeddah belly space returns from Abu Dhabi today, but Riyadh and Dammam stay road-only from the UAE for at least two weeks.

stories.headline: European belly capacity into Dubai builds from 25 November
body: Lufthansa returns with five weekly flights each from Frankfurt and Munich from 25 November, as do SWISS (daily from Zurich) and Eurowings (daily from Berlin). Austrian follows on 12 December. Dubai could gain up to 36 extra weekly European flights by December, but Singapore Airlines, KLM and Air Canada stay out into 2027.
stories.soWhat: Europe–Dubai belly space grows in the peak weeks. Expect softer Europe import rates from late November; Asia lanes stay tight.

stories.headline: UAE firms raise prices at a record pace as freight and fuel costs bite
body: The UAE non-oil PMI eased to 54.8 in October from 55.3. Output prices rose at the fastest rate since the survey began in 2009, and input costs at the fastest since June 2022, driven by fuel, freight, storage and rent.
Dubai's PMI hit an eight-month high of 54.6, and new export orders grew at the quickest rate in two years. S&P Global said firms were passing costs on to customers.
stories.soWhat: Customers are raising their own prices, so the market will accept cost-based rate increases. Use it in renewals.

stories.headline: Dubai will track delivery riders with cameras and sensors, mandatory from H2 2027
body: Dubai's RTA is rolling out cameras and IoT sensors that monitor delivery riders' speed, location, harsh braking and routes, with real-time data for fleet operators. It is voluntary until the end of the first half of 2027, then mandatory for all Dubai delivery companies.
stories.soWhat: A coming cost for every last-mile fleet. Budget the kit and use the data for our own safety and productivity case.

stories.headline: UAE foreign trade keeps double-digit growth through September
body: The Ministry of Foreign Trade says UAE trade grew at double digits in the first nine months of 2026, despite the war. It points to Fujairah and Khorfakkan port investment, Etihad Rail and CEPAs with about 40 countries.
stories.soWhat: Trade volumes are holding up; the fight is over routing and cost, not demand.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Cargo revenue up about 50% in the half year as the war squeezes capacity
body: Emirates SkyCargo carried 1.24 million tonnes from April to September, down 1%, but cargo revenue rose 52% (50% in the standfirst). Emirates said the conflict cut airfreight capacity and pushed shippers from sea to air. It took five new 777 freighters, added Almaty and Zhengzhou, and dnata cargo handling fell 6% to 1.49 million tonnes. Group profit fell 66% as jet fuel doubled.
competitors.soWhat: Air yields are the profit pool right now. Make sure our buy rates and sell rates on SkyCargo lanes reflect the same squeeze.
competitors.imageCredit: Emirates SkyCargo via Air Cargo News

competitors.name: Amazon & noon
competitors.headline: 11.11 sales are live, with 15-minute and 2-hour delivery as the hook
body: Amazon's 11.11 sale runs 5 to 12 November with up to 70% off, free Amazon Now delivery above Dh25 and free 2-hour Rush delivery above Dh100 for Prime. Noon's runs 5 to 13 November with up to 90% off, 15-minute noon Minutes and 90-minute Supermall delivery.
competitors.soWhat: Peak has started two weeks before White Friday, and both platforms sell speed with their own fleets. Our space is the sellers outside their fulfilment.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Regional fuel surcharge for the Middle East held at 18% this week
body: FedEx's Regional Economy fuel surcharge for Middle East, Indian subcontinent and Africa is 18.00% for 2 to 8 November, unchanged every week since January. It is set from Aramco retail diesel. Its domestic rate is 18.5%.
competitors.soWhat: A stable, visible benchmark. Check our regional fuel surcharge sits at or below it before customers compare.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Latest result: record Q2 revenue of AED 1.83bn, up 22%
body: In Q2 2026 Aramex grew revenue 22% to AED 1.83 billion and made net profit of AED 47.4 million, against a loss a year earlier. Freight Forwarding had a record quarter on Europe–Middle East land routing and charters. Domestic Express grew; International Express volumes were broadly stable. Q3 results are not yet out.
competitors.soWhat: Freight and charters are carrying the group. International Express needs the pricing discipline Emirates is showing.

opportunities.title: Cost-based rate increases
opportunities.text: UAE firms are raising prices at a record pace. Customers expect the same from suppliers.

opportunities.title: UAE–Riyadh and Dammam road freight
opportunities.text: Air stays cut to at least 19 November. Keep selling trucking on those lanes.

opportunities.title: Jeddah belly space returns
opportunities.text: Etihad's Jeddah flights restart today. Re-open Abu Dhabi–Jeddah air offers.

opportunities.title: Sea-to-air shift
opportunities.text: Emirates says shippers moved from sea to air. Push sea-air and charter products for Gulf importers.

opportunities.title: Marketplace sellers in peak
opportunities.text: 11.11 is live and White Friday is 27 November. Sell fulfilment and fast delivery to sellers outside Amazon and noon.

watchouts.title: Oil whipsaw
watchouts.text: Brent swung from $94 to $98 in a day. Fuel surcharge promises can go wrong fast.

watchouts.title: Attacks inside the Gulf
watchouts.text: A tanker was hit north of Qatar, not just near Oman. Gulf sea lanes stay high risk.

watchouts.title: Renewed US strikes
watchouts.text: Eurasia Group sees a 60% chance; Brent could reach $110–$125.

watchouts.title: Saudi air extended
watchouts.text: Lufthansa to 30 November, Cathay Riyadh to 31 January. Air capacity to KSA stays short.

watchouts.title: Rider monitoring cost
watchouts.text: Dubai's RTA kit becomes mandatory after H1 2027. Fleet costs will rise.

moves.title: Pause fuel surcharge cuts
moves.text: Brent rebounded to $98. Hold December air and road surcharges until the week's trend is clear.

moves.title: Extend war-risk surcharges to all Gulf sea lanes
moves.text: Attacks now reach waters north of Qatar. Apply them Gulf-wide, not only Gulf of Oman.

moves.title: Re-open Abu Dhabi–Jeddah air
moves.text: Tell shippers who switched to road that Etihad Jeddah flights resume today.

moves.title: Review SkyCargo-lane sell rates
moves.text: Emirates grew cargo revenue ~50% on flat tonnes. Check our margins on the same lanes.

moves.title: Put cost-based increases into renewals
moves.text: Cite the record PMI price rise in November renewal talks.

moves.title: Pitch peak fulfilment to independent sellers
moves.text: 11.11 is live; target sellers not on Amazon or noon fulfilment before White Friday.
